caseStudiesDetail.challenge: When we began at Marriott Santo Domingo, the full-service hotel was technically stabilized but underperforming on mix and margin. Group and transient demand were misaligned, banquet and catering were under-captured relative to competitive set, and the owner lacked a reliable weekly view of revenue, F&B profit, and the actions required to close gaps.
caseStudiesDetail.services: We reset the commercial strategy end to end: rebuilt the group and corporate contracting pipeline, repriced banquet and catering packages, tightened transient channel mix, and instituted a weekly owner reporting cadence that tied revenue actions to GOP and F&B profit drivers—not just occupancy headlines.
caseStudiesDetail.outcome: GOP margin expanded 210 basis points year over year; group room revenue grew 23% while total F&B profit dollars rose 17% in the first full year post-program.
caseStudiesDetail.owner_relevance: Relevant for institutional owners of branded urban full-service hotels in CALA gateway cities evaluating operator-led commercial resets without a full repositioning capex cycle.

caseStudiesDetail.challenge: Courtyard Isla Verde entered the program with aging generator, roof, and public-area systems that had to be renewed without shutting down peak-season demand. The owner needed a capex and operations plan that protected guest safety and cash—and avoided vanity reopen dates that look good on paper but erode RevPAR.
caseStudiesDetail.services: We sequenced generator, roof, and public-area work around forecasted occupancy and event calendars; staged contractor access, guest communication, and contingency operating procedures; and aligned spend releases with lender and owner milestones so each tranche of capex had a clear operating rationale.
caseStudiesDetail.outcome: We sequenced generator, roof, and public-area capex around occupancy so cash and guest safety stayed aligned—no vanity reopen dates. RevPAR versus the owner's chosen competitive set improved 8 points over twelve rolling months; GOP margin expanded 160 bps in the same window as labor productivity improved 7% measured as rooms revenue per paid hour.
caseStudiesDetail.owner_relevance: Reference for select-service owners balancing renovation timing, lender reporting, and operating continuity in airport/leisure submarkets.

caseStudiesDetail.challenge: Independent Bay Villas had a strong beach location but weak pool and beach F&B economics, inconsistent service execution on peak days, and limited repeat-stay capture. Guest reviews cited wait times and menu confusion; owners could not see which outlets and dayparts were destroying margin.
caseStudiesDetail.services: We redesigned beach and pool F&B with simplified menus, standardized prep and service sequences, and labor models tied to forecasted covers by daypart. We retrained beach and kitchen leads, reset vendor and inventory controls, and introduced weekly outlet P&L reviews with the owner.
caseStudiesDetail.outcome: Redesigned beach and pool F&B with simplified menus and labor models tied to peak-day demand; guest satisfaction scores rose 11 points and repeat-stay revenue grew 19% in the first season after rollout.
caseStudiesDetail.owner_relevance: Illustrates independent resort turnaround where owner value is driven by experience and F&B mix—not brand affiliation.
